options: The real unit of compute every Fabric engine spends from a shared pool — a single number representing available compute
A per-item-type separate compute budget
A measure of storage, not compute
A unit only relevant to Eventstreams, not other Fabric engines
questions.explain: Every engine — Spark notebooks, Warehouse queries, Eventstreams — shares the same pool; there's no separate budget per item type.

questions.q: What does an F-SKU (like F64) represent?
options: A fixed number of CUs, purchased as one capacity-level unit
A specific VM size chosen per notebook
A per-item storage limit
A Unity Catalog access control tier
questions.explain: This is Fabric's answer to Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 4's VM-size decision, but chosen once per capacity, not per cluster.

questions.q: What does "bursting" allow a Fabric capacity to do?
options: Briefly use more CUs than the capacity nominally provides, borrowing against future capacity
Permanently increase the capacity's CU budget with no limit
Skip billing entirely for a short period
Disable smoothing temporarily
questions.explain: This means an occasional heavy job doesn't automatically require a permanently bigger SKU.

options: Spreads a job's real cost out over time, rather than charging a spike all at once
Reduces the total number of CUs a job can ever use
Converts CUs into a different billing currency
Only applies to Warehouse queries, never Spark jobs
questions.explain: Together with bursting, this means sizing depends on sustained average load, not worst-case peaks.

questions.q: Why doesn't an occasional heavy job automatically require buying a larger F-SKU?
options: Bursting and smoothing exist specifically so occasional heavy work doesn't force permanently paying for peak-load-sized compute
Heavy jobs are always rejected regardless of capacity size
F-SKUs automatically resize themselves permanently after any heavy job
There's no real relationship between job size and capacity sizing
questions.explain: This mirrors the same cost-awareness point Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 5 made about job clusters vs. all-purpose clusters.
